key_concept: Placentation is the arrangement of ovules inside the ovary, and each type has a standard NCERT example: marginal (pea), axile (tomato, china rose, lemon), parietal (mustard, Argemone) and free central (Dianthus, Primrose).
steps: A. Marginal placentation: the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of a unilocular (monocarpellary) ovary, and the ovules sit in two rows. Example: Pea (Fabaceae), so A–IV.
B. Axile placentation: the placenta is axial in a multilocular syncarpous ovary, and the ovules attach to the central axis. Examples: Tomato, china rose, lemon, so B–II.

C. Parietal placentation: the ovules develop on the inner wall (periphery) of a unilocular ovary. It becomes two-chambered in mustard due to a false septum (replum). Examples: Argemone, mustard, so C–I.
D. Free central placentation: the ovules are borne on a central axis, and septa are absent. Examples: Dianthus, Primrose, so D–III.
The correct matching is A–IV, B–II, C–I, D–III, which is Option (4) and agrees with the NTA key.
why_not_others: Option (1) gives marginal placentation to tomato, but tomato is axile. Option (2) swaps Primrose and Argemone between parietal and free central. Option (3) wrongly gives axile placentation to Primrose and free central placentation to tomato.
common_trap: Students confuse parietal with free central placentation because both occur in unilocular ovaries. Remember that the ovules are on the wall in parietal (Argemone) and on a central column without septa in free central (Primrose).
time_saving_tip: Pea = marginal is the most certain pair and removes option (1). Then Tomato = axile removes option (3), and Argemone = parietal removes option (2), leaving option (4).
